description: Search query construction and limits shared by SQLiteSearchIndex (macOS) and SearchIndex (Windows). `queryTerms` splits on any text element that is not a letter, a number or '_' (a combining mark stays with its base letter), keeps at most 16 terms and the first 128 characters of each. `ftsQuery` quotes every term (doubling embedded quotes), adds a prefix star and joins with AND; no terms means no FTS query and content search falls back to filename search. `escapedLike` escapes backslash, percent and underscore for LIKE ... ESCAPE '\'. Limits clamp into 1...500. The index is SQLite FTS5 with tokenizer `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`.
behaviour: Filename search matches the query as a case-insensitive substring of the relative path (SQLite NOCASE folds ASCII only); prefix matches rank first, then shorter paths, then path order.

Content search streams two batches: an unranked first batch (score 0, at most 20 results) then a final batch ranked by bm25 with ties broken by relative path. Filename search streams one batch unless the first batch was full and the limit is larger.
Each content result carries an excerpt of at most 1024 characters starting 240 characters before the first occurrence of the first term.
When no workspace filter is set, one physical file reached through overlapping workspace roots appears once, attributed to the workspace with the longest root.
Files larger than 50 MiB, non-UTF-8 files and files that change into a link after scanning are not indexed.
